title: The Effects of Menstrual Cycle Phase on Exercise Performance in Eumenorrheic Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: McNulty KL, Elliott-Sale KJ, Dolan E, Swinton PA, Ansdell P, Goodall S, Thomas K, Hicks KM
population: Eumenorrheic women in experimental studies measuring exercise performance in two or more menstrual cycle phases
findings: 78 studies included; 51 eligible for the pairwise meta-analysis and 73 for the network meta-analysis.
Pooled effect: trivial reduction in performance in the early follicular phase versus all other phases for both endurance and strength outcomes (ES0.5 = -0.06, 95% CrI -0.16 to 0.04).
Largest pairwise effect was early follicular vs late follicular (ES0.5 = -0.14, 95% CrI -0.26 to -0.03). SUCRA was 30% for the early follicular phase and 53-55% for all other phases.

Quality of evidence graded low (42%). Authors state general guidelines cannot be formed because of trivial effect size, large between-study variation and poor-quality studies, and recommend a personalised approach based on each individual's response.
limitations: Low overall study quality, large between-study variance, small samples and heterogeneous phase verification. Pooled credible interval includes zero.
implications: Apply no population-level cycle-phase multiplier to session intensity or volume.

If cycle tracking is offered, use it as an optional individual annotation (symptoms and session quality by phase); surface her own pattern only after at least 3 logged cycles (design default); never auto-reduce or move key sessions or race pacing from phase alone.
Do not schedule races or key workouts around cycle phase by default.

verification.notes: Crossref matches title, Sports Medicine, 2020, first author McNulty. All numbers confirmed in the Europe PMC abstract (PMID 32661839).
